description: Bring the web dashboard (landing/dashboard/) to full feature parity with the iOS app. Add Events browsing, Settlement view, Event Detail with batch grading, Dashboard enhancements, CSV export for organizers. Add complete player (member) web app: dual-role auth routing, player home with balance and performance, events browsing with bet placement (bet slip), pick tracking, and player account/settings. All changes in landing/dashboard/ files: app.html, dashboard.js, dashboard.css, index.html.

userStories.title: Add Events tab with sport browsing and search
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to browse events/games by sport and search by team name on the web dashboard, so I can see what games are available and check odds.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Events' link to sidebar navigation between Picks and Subscription, with a calendar/game icon SVG
Add route handling for '#/events' in parseRoute(), loading events data when navigated to
Add 'events' to the valid routes list so it doesn't redirect to dashboard
Create async loadEvents() method that fetches from Supabase 'events' table where bookie_id IS NULL, ordered by start_time ascending, limited to events with start_time >= 14 days ago
Add state variables: events (array), isLoadingEvents (boolean), eventSearch (string), eventSportFilter (string, default '')
Create events view HTML section with x-show="route === 'events'"
Add page header: 'Events' title with subtitle showing event count
Add search input (class 'search-input') that filters events by home_team or away_team (case-insensitive)
Add sport filter chips: All, Football, Basketball, Baseball, Hockey, Soccer, Golf, MMA, Tennis — using existing .chip and .chip.active CSS classes
Add computed getter 'filteredEvents' that filters by search query AND sport filter, then sorts by start_time ascending
Group events by sport + league with section headers (styled like card-header with sport name and league)

Each event row shows: start_time (formatted), away_team @ home_team, status badge (scheduled=badge-muted, in_progress=badge-warning, final=badge-success, canceled=badge-danger), and is clickable to navigate to '#/events/{id}'
Add shimmer loading skeleton while events are loading (3 skeleton rows)
Add empty state when no events match filters: 'No events found' with description
Events with status 'final' that are older than 48 hours should be hidden unless search is active
Responsive: event rows use flexbox and stack on mobile (below 768px)
userStories.notes: Events are shared (bookie_id IS NULL). Query with .is('bookie_id', null) or .or('bookie_id.is.null'). Sport values in DB: americanfootball_nfl, basketball_nba, baseball_mlb, icehockey_nhl, soccer_epl, golf_pga, mma_ufc, tennis_atp — map these to display names. The iOS app uses SportCategory enum for sport display names.

userStories.title: Add Event Detail view with odds, exposure, and pick management
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to view event details including odds, exposure breakdown, and all picks placed on the event, so I can manage risk and grade picks.
acceptanceCriteria: Add route handling for '#/events/{id}' in parseRoute() — pattern: /^events\/(.+)$/
Add state: selectedEventId, eventDetail (null), eventDetailBets (array), eventDetailMarkets (array), isLoadingEventDetail (boolean)

Create async loadEventDetail() that fetches the event by ID, its markets (from 'markets' table where event_id matches), and all bets placed on this event (from 'bets' table where event_id matches and bookie_id matches)
Create event-detail view HTML with x-show="route === 'event-detail'"
Back button: 'Back to Events' linking to '#/events'
Hero card showing: status badge (large), start_time, matchup (away_team @ home_team), sport + league, final_score if status is 'final'

Markets card showing available odds: for each market, show market type (Moneyline/Spread/Total using formatMarketType), home odds, away odds, and for totals show over/under line. Style odds in monospace font. Markets are view-only (no bet placement)
Exposure Breakdown card: group bets by side, show count of bets and total stake per side, highlight the side with higher exposure in accent color. Show total exposure across all sides
Picks card: table of all bets on this event with columns: Member (linked to member detail), Side, Odds, Stake, Status badge. Rows clickable to pick detail. Use existing data-table pattern
Add shimmer loading state for event detail
If event has no bets, show empty state in Picks card: 'No picks placed on this event'
If event has no markets, show empty state in Markets card: 'No odds available'
userStories.notes: Markets table columns: id, event_id, bookie_id, market_type (h2h/spreads/totals/outright), home_odds, away_odds, draw_odds, over_line, under_line, spread_line, over_odds, under_odds, home_spread_odds, away_spread_odds, updated_at. Markets have bookie_id NULL for shared markets. Event IDs in bets table are stored as TEXT (event_id column), not UUID — use string comparison.

userStories.title: Add batch grading and event management actions to Event Detail
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to change event status, enter final scores, and batch grade all picks on an event, so I can efficiently manage game results.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Actions card to event detail view (only shown when event has bets with gradable statuses: accepted, readyToGrade)

Grade All Picks section: Win (Home) / Win (Away) / Push buttons using existing .btn-grade, .btn-grade-win, .btn-grade-loss, .btn-grade-push CSS classes. Clicking a button opens a confirmation modal showing how many picks will be graded

Grade confirmation modal: 'Grade X picks as [outcome]?' with Cancel and Confirm buttons. On confirm, call grade_bet edge function for each eligible bet in sequence (not parallel, to respect rate limits). Show progress: 'Grading pick X of Y...' Toast success/error counts when done
Void All Picks button (btn-danger-outline): confirmation modal 'Void all X active picks on this event?'. Calls grade_bet with outcome 'void' for each eligible bet

Add Enter Final Score action: button opens modal with two number inputs (Away Score, Home Score). On save, updates event in Supabase: final_score as 'away_score-home_score' string format, status to 'final'. Toast on success
Add Change Status action: dropdown with options Scheduled, Live, Final, Postponed, Canceled. Updates event status in Supabase. When changing to Canceled, show confirmation warning about voiding picks
After any grading action completes, reload event detail data to refresh pick statuses
All grade_bet calls include idempotency_key: crypto.randomUUID()
userStories.notes: Eligible bets for grading: status in ['accepted', 'readyToGrade']. Eligible bets for voiding: status in ['pending', 'accepted', 'readyToGrade']. The grade_bet edge function expects { bet_id, outcome, idempotency_key } where outcome is 'win', 'loss', 'push', or 'void'. Do NOT grade bets that are already settled/graded/void.

userStories.title: Add Settlement view with weekly periods and per-member reports
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need a settlement view showing weekly settlement periods with per-member balance reports and mark-paid actions, so I can track collections and manage weekly settle-ups.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Settlement' as a navigable card/link on the Dashboard view (inside a card with calendar icon, similar to iOS SettlementSnapshotCard). Clicking navigates to '#/settlement'
Add route handling for '#/settlement' in parseRoute()
Add state: settlementWeek (Date, default to most recent Sunday), isLoadingSettlement (boolean), settlementReports (array)
Create helper function mostRecentSunday() that returns the most recent Sunday (if today is Sunday, return today). Week runs Monday through Sunday
Create week selector: left/right arrow buttons to navigate weeks, showing date range 'Mon MMM D - Sun MMM D, YYYY'. Limit to last 5 weeks (no future navigation)

Create async loadSettlement() that calculates per-member settlement reports for the selected week: for each active member, sum ledger entries within the week period to get starting balance, bets won/lost amounts, adjustments, and ending balance
Settlement summary row at top: 'Owed to You' total (sum of positive ending balances) in accent color, 'You Owe' total (sum of negative ending balances, shown as positive) in danger color
Filter chips: All, Unsettled (ending balance != 0 and not marked paid), Settled (marked paid or zero balance), Needs Attention (overdue collection status)
Per-member settlement table with columns: Member (linked), Starting Balance, Won, Lost, Adjustments, Ending Balance (color-coded), Status (Settled/Unpaid badge), Actions
Mark Paid action button per member: calls adjust_balance edge function with type 'paymentLogged' and amount that zeroes the balance. Show confirmation with amount. Toast on success, reload settlement
Settlement view uses existing card, data-table, badge, chip, and filter-bar CSS patterns
Add shimmer skeleton while loading
Empty state when no members have activity for the selected week
userStories.notes: Settlement calculation: starting_balance = sum of ledger_entries before week start for that player. Bets won/lost = sum of settlement-type ledger entries within the week. Adjustments = sum of adjustment-type ledger entries within the week. Ending balance = starting_balance + bets_won_lost + adjustments. The adjust_balance edge function expects { player_id, amount, type, reason, idempotency_key }. For Mark Paid: amount should negate the ending balance (if player owes $100, send amount: -100 with type: 'paymentLogged').

userStories.title: Add CSV export for settlement reports
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to export settlement reports as CSV files, so I can keep records and share reports outside the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Export CSV' button (btn-ghost with download icon) to the settlement view header, next to the week selector
Clicking generates a CSV file from the current settlementReports data
CSV columns: Member Name, Starting Balance, Bets Won, Bets Lost, Adjustments, Ending Balance, Status (Settled/Unpaid)
CSV header row uses these exact column names
Currency values formatted as plain numbers (no $ symbol) with 2 decimal places for CSV compatibility
Add summary row at bottom: 'TOTAL', sum of each numeric column, empty status
File name format: 'booki-settlement-YYYY-MM-DD.csv' where date is the week ending Sunday
Download triggers via creating a Blob with text/csv MIME type, creating an object URL, clicking a temporary <a> element, then revoking the URL
Toast 'Settlement report exported' on success
Button disabled when settlementReports is empty or loading
userStories.notes: Standard browser CSV download pattern: const blob = new Blob([csvString], { type: 'text/csv' }); const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = url; a.download = filename; a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url);

userStories.title: Add Attention Feed card to Dashboard
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to see urgent alerts on the dashboard (overdue members, near credit limit, high exposure) so I can take action on issues that need attention.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Attention Feed card to dashboard, positioned above the Members Grid section
Card header: 'Attention' with count badge showing total alert count
Three alert categories sorted by severity: Overdue (red, urgent), Near Credit Limit (red, urgent), High Exposure Games (orange, warning)
Overdue alerts: members with collection_status === 'overdue' — show member name, balance owed, 'Overdue' badge in danger color. Row clickable to member detail
Near Credit Limit alerts: members with credit utilization >= 75% — show member name, utilization percentage, 'Near Limit' badge in danger color. Row clickable to member detail

High Exposure alerts: identify from open bets — events where total bookie exposure (sum of potential payouts minus stakes for open bets) >= $500. Show event name, exposure amount, 'High Exposure' badge in warning color
Each alert row has an icon (exclamation triangle for urgent, warning triangle for warning), description text, and right-aligned amount or percentage
When no alerts exist, show 'All clear — no issues need attention' with a checkmark icon in accent color
Use computed getter 'attentionAlerts' that builds the array from existing dashboard data (players, bets, allLedgerEntries)
Card collapsible: show max 5 alerts with 'View All (X)' toggle when more exist
Alerts should use existing styling: card background, border-left colored by severity (4px solid var(--danger) or var(--warning))
userStories.notes: Credit utilization is calculated as abs(balance) / credit_limit * 100. Balance comes from ledger entries sum for that player. The dashboard already loads allLedgerEntries and players, so this data is available. High exposure requires iterating open bets and grouping by event_id.

userStories.title: Add Tonight's Exposure card to Dashboard
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to see tonight's game exposure at a glance on the dashboard, so I can quickly assess my risk for today's games.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Tonight's Open Activity card to dashboard, positioned after the stats grid and before the Attention Feed
Card header: 'Tonight's Open Activity' with a clock icon
Show total games count for tonight (events with start_time between now and end of today, status not final/canceled)
Show Total Potential Loss: sum of (potential_return - stake) for all open bets on tonight's events. Color-coded in danger
Show Highest Risk Game: the event with the largest total exposure, showing matchup name, start time, and exposure amount
If exposure exceeds $1,000 on any single game, show a 'High Exposure' badge in warning color
If no games tonight, show 'No games scheduled tonight' in muted text
Card clickable — navigates to '#/events' filtered to today
Compute tonight's events by comparing event start_time to today's date range (midnight to midnight in local timezone)
Use existing stat-tile-like layout for the metrics inside the card
Add computed getter 'tonightsExposure' that returns { gameCount, totalPotentialLoss, highestRiskGame, highExposure }
userStories.notes: Potential return calculation from American odds: positive odds → stake * (odds/100), negative odds → stake * (100/abs(odds)). The potential loss to the bookie is potential_return (not including stake return). Tonight's events: filter events where start_time is today (use local date comparison). Open bets: status in ['pending', 'accepted'].

userStories.title: Add Member Risk Watchlist card to Dashboard
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to see which members have the most risk signals so I can proactively manage my book.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Risk Watchlist card to dashboard, positioned after the Attention Feed and before Members Grid
Card header: 'Risk Watchlist' with shield icon
Show top 5 members with risk signals, sorted by number of signals descending

Risk signals (as small badges per member row): 'Near Limit' (credit utilization >= 75%, danger color), 'Overdue' (collection_status === 'overdue', danger color), 'Hot Streak' (3+ consecutive wins, warning color), 'Losing Big' (net P/L worse than -$500 in last 7 days, danger color)
Each member row shows: name, credit utilization progress bar (same style as members grid), risk badges, and balance amount
Member rows clickable — navigate to member detail
Only show the card if at least one member has a risk signal
Pro-gated: wrap in pro-gated-section with blur overlay for free tier
Use computed getter 'riskWatchlist' that returns top 5 members with signals array
Use existing credit utilization bar styles (progress bar with fill, warning color at >80%)
userStories.notes: Hot streak detection: sort member's graded bets by created_at descending, count consecutive wins from the top. Losing big: sum ledger entries (excluding paymentLogged) from last 7 days. Credit utilization calculation already exists in getMemberCreditUtilization(). The dashboard already computes attention tags — some of this data can be reused.

userStories.title: Add Settlement Snapshot card to Dashboard
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need a quick settlement overview on the dashboard showing current week totals and top unpaid members, so I can track collections without leaving the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Settlement Snapshot card to dashboard, positioned after the Risk Watchlist
Card header: 'Settlement' with calendar icon, showing current week date range (Mon MMM D - Sun MMM D, YYYY) as subtitle
Show two metrics side by side: 'Owed to You' (sum of positive member balances, accent color) and 'You Owe' (sum of negative member balances shown as positive, danger color)
Show stats row: 'X unpaid' count with person icon, 'X overdue' count with warning icon
Show top 3 unpaid members (highest balance first): member name, amount owed (color-coded), and 'Mark Paid' button per row
Mark Paid button: calls adjust_balance edge function with type 'paymentLogged' to zero the balance. Show brief 'Paid' confirmation with checkmark animation, then refresh data
Bottom link: 'View Settlements' navigating to '#/settlement' (styled like btn-ghost with chevron right, accent background at 10% opacity)
If overdue count > 0, show 'X overdue' badge (capsule, danger background) in the card header
Use existing card, badge, and button patterns
Compute from allLedgerEntries and players data already loaded on dashboard
userStories.notes: This mirrors the iOS SettlementSnapshotCard. Balances come from summing all ledger entries per player (the allLedgerEntries array is already fetched on dashboard load). Unpaid = positive balance and not recently paid. Overdue = player.collection_status === 'overdue'. The 'Mark Paid' quick action is the same as settle up — calls adjust_balance with negated balance amount and type paymentLogged.

userStories.title: Add notification preferences to Settings
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to manage my notification preferences from the web dashboard settings, so I can control which notifications I receive.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Notifications' section to Settings view, positioned after Change Password section
Section header: 'Notifications' with bell icon
Show toggle switches for each notification type: New Members (default true), Pick Submissions (default false), Risk Alerts (default true), Game Results (default true)
On settings load, fetch notification_preferences from Supabase for the current user. If no record exists, use defaults
Each toggle change immediately updates the notification_preferences record in Supabase (upsert pattern). Toast on success
Use existing toggle-row, toggle-switch, toggle-label, toggle-desc CSS classes

Add description text under each toggle explaining what it controls: New Members = 'When a member accepts your invite', Pick Submissions = 'When a member places a pick', Risk Alerts = 'Credit limit and exposure warnings', Game Results = 'When games are graded and picks are settled'
Add state: notifPrefs object with boolean fields, isLoadingNotifPrefs boolean
Load notification preferences in loadSettings() method
userStories.notes: notification_preferences table columns: user_id (unique), picks_graded, balance_changes, new_members, pick_submissions, game_results, risk_alerts, marketing. The web dashboard maps: New Members = new_members, Pick Submissions = pick_submissions, Risk Alerts = risk_alerts, Game Results = game_results. Upsert pattern: this.supabase.from('notification_preferences').upsert({ user_id: this.session.user.id, [field]: value }, { onConflict: 'user_id' }).

userStories.title: Add accept/decline actions for pending picks on Dashboard
userStories.description: As an organizer with manual approval enabled, I need to accept or decline pending picks directly from the dashboard, so I can manage picks without navigating to the pick detail page.
acceptanceCriteria: On the dashboard Recent Activity section, add Accept/Decline action buttons on pending pick rows (bets with status 'pending')
Accept button (btn-grade-win style, compact): calls accept_bet edge function with { bet_id, idempotency_key }. On success, toast 'Pick accepted' and reload dashboard

Decline button (btn-grade-loss style, compact): opens a confirmation modal 'Decline this pick?' with optional reason input. Calls decline_bet edge function with { bet_id, reason, idempotency_key }. On success, toast 'Pick declined' and reload dashboard
Buttons only shown when organizer has manual_bet_acceptance enabled (check bookie settings)
Buttons are compact (small font, minimal padding) to fit inline with activity rows
Add state: acceptingBetId (string, null), decliningBetId (string, null) for loading states on individual rows
Disable buttons while action is in progress, show spinner or 'Accepting...' text
Also add Accept/Decline buttons on the Picks tab for pending picks — small action buttons in the status column
userStories.notes: accept_bet edge function expects { bet_id, idempotency_key }. decline_bet expects { bet_id, reason?, idempotency_key }. The bookie's manual_bet_acceptance setting is on the bookies table — load it with the bookie record. Most organizers use auto-accept (default), so this is lower priority.

userStories.title: Add acceptance policy settings
userStories.description: As an organizer, I need to configure acceptance policy rules from the web dashboard, so I can set max stake limits and auto-decline rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Acceptance Rules' subsection within Pick Management settings (Pro-gated)
Show current rules from acceptance_policies table (fetch by bookie_id)

Editable fields: Max Stake (number input, optional — null means no limit), Require Approval Above (number input, optional — bets above this amount need manual approval), Event Lock Offset (number input, minutes before game start to stop accepting picks, default 0)
Auto-Accept toggles: Auto-Accept Enabled (master toggle), Auto-Accept New Players (toggle), Auto-Accept Parlays (toggle)
Parlay Max Legs (number input, only shown when Auto-Accept Parlays is on)
Save button: upserts acceptance_policies record in Supabase. Toast on success
If no acceptance_policies record exists for this bookie, show all defaults and create on first save
Pro-gated: entire section blurred with upgrade overlay for free tier
Use existing form-group, toggle-row patterns
Add state: acceptancePolicy object, isLoadingAcceptancePolicy boolean, isSavingAcceptancePolicy boolean
userStories.notes: acceptance_policies table: bookie_id (UNIQUE), max_stake, require_approval_above, auto_accept_enabled (default true), auto_accept_new_players (default true), auto_accept_parlays (default true), parlay_max_legs, event_lock_offset_minutes (default 0), parlay_push_void_policy. Load in loadSettings(). Upsert with onConflict: 'bookie_id'.

userStories.title: Add dual-role auth routing for player and organizer login
userStories.description: As a player (member), I need to log in to the web dashboard and be routed to a player experience, so I can view my picks, balance, and place bets from a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify index.html login flow: remove the isOrganizer() gate that rejects non-organizer logins. Instead, after login, determine user role and route accordingly

Role detection logic: (1) check if user has a bookie record in bookies table — if yes and not a spurious record, route as organizer. (2) check if user has a player record in players table with a bookie_id — if yes, route as player. (3) if neither, create a standalone player experience (synthetic bookie not needed for web — just show events and track)
Add state variable: userRole ('organizer' | 'player' | 'standalone'), playerId (string), playerBookieId (string)
For player login: fetch the player record to get player.id, player.bookie_id, player.credit_limit, player.name. Store in state
For player login: also fetch the bookie record for the player's bookie_id to get bookie settings (allow_futures_parlays, tier, etc.)
Update sidebar navigation: organizers see Dashboard/Members/Picks/Events/Settlement/Subscription/Settings. Players see Home/Games/Track/Account. Use x-show on sidebar links based on userRole
Update parseRoute() to validate routes against user role — players can't access #/members, organizers can't access #/player-home
Player routes: #/player-home, #/player-games, #/player-track, #/player-account, #/player-ticket/{id}
Update app.html page title and mobile header to show role-appropriate branding
Sign-up flow: new sign-ups always create an organizer (bookie) record — same as current behavior. Players are created via invite flow only
userStories.notes: The existing isOrganizer() function in index.html handles spurious bookie records well — keep that logic but extend it. For players: query players table where auth_user_id = userId. The player's bookie_id tells us which organizer they belong to. Standalone users (no player record, no bookie record) should see a limited experience — just events browsing and a prompt to either become an organizer or enter an invite code. The Supabase session/token is the same for both roles — role is determined by which tables have records.

userStories.title: Add player home view with balance, performance, and recent activity
userStories.description: As a player, I need a home screen showing my current balance, performance stats, and recent activity, so I can see my status at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Create player home view HTML with x-show="route === 'player-home' && userRole === 'player'"

Balance hero section at top: large balance number (styled like Account hero in iOS — 32pt+ bold), color-coded green (positive = bookie owes you) or red (negative = you owe). Context text below: 'Amount owed to you' / 'Amount you owe' / 'All settled'. Disclaimer text: 'Balances are informational and not processed by Booki.'
Balance calculation: fetch all ledger_entries for this player_id, sum amounts, then NEGATE for display (internal positive = player owes bookie, display positive = credit owed to player)
Performance card: Record (W-L-P) in large colored numbers with dots (green wins, red losses, gray pushes), Win Rate percentage, Net Performance (P/L, color-coded), Open Picks count

Credit utilization bar: shows used/total credit. Available credit = credit_limit - abs(balance) - open_stakes. Color-coded progress bar (teal <50%, gold 50-80%, orange 80-100%, red 100%+). Hidden for standalone users

Recent Activity section: last 10 ledger entries for this player, showing description, date, amount (player-facing: negated), type badge. Settlement entries show bet context (e.g., 'Won - Lakers ML -150')
Add async loadPlayerHome() that fetches player's ledger entries, bets (for record calc), and current balance
Add computed getters: playerBalance, playerRecord (W-L-P from grade_result), playerWinRate, playerPnl, playerOpenPicks, playerCreditUtilization
Shimmer loading skeleton while data loads
Load player home data on init and on route navigation
userStories.notes: Balance convention: internal positive = player owes bookie. For player display, NEGATE the value so positive = credit (green), negative = debt (red). This is critical. Open stakes = sum of stakes for bets with status in ['pending', 'accepted']. Credit utilization = (abs(balance) + open_stakes) / credit_limit * 100. The player's bets and ledger entries are already filtered by player_id in the Supabase query.

userStories.title: Add player games view with odds browsing and bet selection
userStories.description: As a player, I need to browse upcoming games with odds and select picks to add to my bet slip, so I can place bets from the web.
acceptanceCriteria: Create player games view HTML with x-show="route === 'player-games' && userRole === 'player'"
Fetch events from Supabase: events where bookie_id IS NULL, status NOT IN ('final', 'canceled'), start_time > now, ordered by start_time ascending
Also fetch markets for all displayed events: markets where bookie_id IS NULL or event_id in displayed event IDs
Sport filter tabs at top: horizontal scrollable chips for All + each sport with events. Active chip styled with accent background
Search input to filter by team name (home_team or away_team)
Group events by sport + league with section headers showing 'SPREAD / MONEY / TOTAL' column labels
Each game row shows: start time, away team name + 3 odds buttons (spread, moneyline, total/over-under), home team name + 3 odds buttons. Modeled after iOS CompactGameRow layout
Odds buttons show the odds value (e.g., '-110', '+150') with spread/total line where applicable (e.g., '-3.5 -110'). Styled as small tappable pills with border
Clicking an odds button toggles that selection into the bet slip (adds or removes). Selected buttons have accent background. Store selections in a betSlipSelections array
Each selection stores: event_id, market_id, side (human-readable team name + market), side_indicator ('a' or 'b'), odds (number), event_name (away @ home), market_type
Floating bet slip indicator at bottom of page (fixed position): shows '[N] Selection(s)' in accent bar when selections exist. Clicking opens bet slip modal
Lock detection: if event start_time has passed, show odds as locked (muted, non-clickable) with lock icon
Empty state when no upcoming games: 'No upcoming games' with description
Shimmer skeleton while events load
Add state: playerEvents (array), playerMarkets (array), betSlipSelections (array), isLoadingPlayerEvents (boolean), playerEventSearch (string), playerSportFilter (string)
userStories.notes: Markets table: market_type (h2h/spreads/totals/outright), home_odds, away_odds, spread_line, home_spread_odds, away_spread_odds, over_line, over_odds, under_odds. For the game row: Spread column uses home_spread_odds/away_spread_odds with spread_line. Money column uses home_odds/away_odds (h2h market). Total column uses over_odds/under_odds with over_line. side_indicator 'a' = away/over, 'b' = home/under for the submit_bets edge function. Group markets by event_id for O(1) lookup. Market IDs must be stored in selections for submission.

userStories.title: Add bet slip modal with singles and multi-pick submission
userStories.description: As a player, I need a bet slip where I can enter stakes for my selections and submit picks, so I can place singles and multi-pick bets from the web.
acceptanceCriteria: Create bet slip as a modal overlay (full-height slide-up on mobile, right-side panel or centered modal on desktop)
Modal header: 'Pick Entry' title, Close button, Clear All button (danger text)
Mode toggle: Singles / Multi tabs (capsule segmented control). Multi disabled when fewer than 2 selections. Multi disabled if bookie doesn't allow futures parlays and selections contain futures
Available credit display: show '$X,XXX max' (available_credit = credit_limit - abs(balance) - open_stakes)
Selection cards: each shows event name, side/pick description, odds. X button to remove. In singles mode, each card has a Stake input field
Stake input fields: number inputs with $ prefix, step 0.01. On change, calculate To Win amount displayed next to it
To Win calculation: positive odds → stake * (odds/100), negative odds → stake * (100/abs(odds))
Quick stake buttons: +$1, +$5, +$25 — adds to current active stake field
Multi-pick mode: single stake input at bottom, combined odds displayed (multiply decimal odds of all legs), combined To Win
Combined odds calculation: for each leg convert American to decimal (positive: 1 + odds/100, negative: 1 + 100/abs(odds)), multiply all, convert back to American
Validation: stake > 0, total stakes don't exceed available credit, no locked events. Show warning text when validation fails. Disable Place Pick button when invalid
Place Pick button: full-width accent button at bottom. Text: 'Place Pick' (single) / 'Place Picks' (multiple singles) / 'Place Multi-Pick' (parlay). Dimmed when disabled
Singles submission: calls submit_bets edge function with { player_id, bookie_id, bets: [{event_id, market_id, side, odds, stake}], idempotency_key }
Multi-pick submission: calls submit_parlay edge function with { player_id, bookie_id, stake, combined_odds, legs: [{event_id, market_id, side, side_indicator, odds}], idempotency_key }
Loading state during submission: overlay with spinner, disable all inputs
Success state: checkmark animation with randomized confirmation message (pick from array of 10+ fun messages like 'Locked in!', 'Let it ride!', 'Good luck!'). Done button to dismiss
Error handling: toast error message, keep bet slip open so user can retry
After successful submission: clear selections, close bet slip, reload player data (balance, open picks)
Add state: showBetSlip (boolean), betSlipMode ('singles' | 'multi'), betSlipStakes (object keyed by selection index), isSubmittingBets (boolean), betSlipSuccess (boolean)
Compliance disclaimer at bottom of bet slip: 'Picks are not processed as real-money wagers by Booki.'
Add CSS for bet slip modal: .bet-slip-overlay, .bet-slip-modal, .bet-slip-header, .bet-slip-card, .odds-pill, .odds-pill.selected
userStories.notes: submit_bets expects: { player_id, bookie_id, bets: [{ event_id, market_id, side, odds, stake }], idempotency_key }. submit_parlay expects: { player_id, bookie_id, stake, combined_odds, legs: [{ event_id, market_id, side, side_indicator, odds }], idempotency_key }. The side field should be human-readable (e.g., 'Lakers -3.5'). side_indicator is 'a' (away/over) or 'b' (home/under). Both functions return { success: true, results: [...] } with partial success model for singles. Available credit must be fetched via get_player_balance RPC or calculated from ledger + open bets.

userStories.title: Add player track view for viewing open and past picks
userStories.description: As a player, I need to view my open and past picks with performance stats, so I can track my betting history and results.
acceptanceCriteria: Create player track view HTML with x-show="route === 'player-track' && userRole === 'player'"
Summary card at top: Record (W-L-P), Total Staked, Net Performance (P/L, color-coded green/red). Use stat-tile-like layout
Filter chips: All (N), Open (N), Won (N), Lost (N), Pushed (N). Counts computed from player's bets. Use existing .chip and .chip.active classes
Open = status in ['pending', 'accepted', 'readyToGrade', 'graded']. Won = settled + grade_result 'win'. Lost = settled + grade_result 'loss'. Pushed = settled + grade_result 'push'

Ticket cards for each pick/ticket: group bets by ticket_id (parlays share ticket_id, singles have unique ticket_id). Each card shows: title (e.g., 'Lakers ML -150' for singles, '3-leg Multi-Pick +450' for parlays), status badge, stake, profit/potential return
For settled singles: show final score (away_score - home_score) if available from the event
For multi-picks: show colored status dots per leg (teal=win, red=loss, yellow=push, gray=pending/void)
Cards clickable — navigate to '#/player-ticket/{ticket_id}' (use first bet's ID for singles)
Fetch player's bets from Supabase: bets where player_id = playerId, ordered by created_at descending
Also fetch events for bet enrichment (event names, final scores) — batch fetch by event_id
Add computed getter 'playerTickets' that groups bets by ticket_id into ticket objects with calculated combined odds for parlays
Add computed getter 'playerTrackStats' for the summary card
Add computed getter 'filteredPlayerTickets' that filters by selected track filter
Add state: playerBets (array), playerTrackFilter ('all'), isLoadingPlayerTrack (boolean)
Empty state: 'No Picks Yet' with description encouraging browsing games
Pull-to-refresh equivalent: refresh button in header that reloads data
userStories.notes: Ticket grouping: bets with the same ticket_id are legs of a parlay. Singles have a unique ticket_id (or null — treat null ticket_id as standalone). Combined parlay odds: multiply decimal odds of all legs, convert back to American. Profit calculation: Win → potential_return based on odds. Loss → -stake. Push → 0. For parlays: all legs must be graded to determine ticket result. If any leg is a loss, ticket is a loss. If all are win/push, calculate combined odds excluding pushed legs.

userStories.title: Add player ticket detail view
userStories.description: As a player, I need to view the full details of a pick including odds, stake, potential return, and leg details for multi-picks.
acceptanceCriteria: Create player ticket detail view HTML with x-show="route === 'player-ticket' && userRole === 'player'"
Add route handling for '#/player-ticket/{id}' in parseRoute()
Back button: 'Back to Track' linking to '#/player-track'
Hero card: title (side for singles, 'X-leg Multi-Pick' for parlays), status badge (large), event name (away @ home), sport/league, date placed. For singles: show final score if available
For multi-picks: show each leg as a row with side, odds, event name, league, and grade result badge (won/lost/push/pending). Colored dot indicator per leg
Financials card: Stake, Odds (formatted American), Potential Return (if open) or Profit + Total Return (if settled). Color-code profit green/red
Odds format: show American by default (e.g., +150, -110). For parlays show combined odds
Activity card: show 'Placed' date with 'Pick placed' description. If graded, show graded date and result. Simple timeline with dots and lines (matching existing pick detail pattern)
Fetch bet(s) by ID or ticket_id, enrich with event data
Add state: playerTicketDetail (null), playerTicketLegs (array), isLoadingPlayerTicket (boolean)
Shimmer loading while data loads
userStories.notes: For singles: fetch single bet by ID. For parlays: fetch all bets with matching ticket_id. Enrich with event data by fetching from events table using event_id. The existing pick detail view (organizer) has similar structure — reuse the card layout patterns but without the grading actions. Player-facing amounts: profit is displayed as-is (positive = player won money, negative = player lost money), no negation needed since these are relative to the player's perspective.

userStories.title: Add player account view with profile, settings, and activity
userStories.description: As a player, I need an account page to view my profile, change my password, view transaction history, and manage my account.
acceptanceCriteria: Create player account view HTML with x-show="route === 'player-account' && userRole === 'player'"

Profile section (card): show Name (read-only), Email (read-only), Organizer name (fetched from bookie record), Member Since date. 'Edit Profile' link that opens inline editing for name (saves to players table display_name or name)

Change Password section: same as organizer — current password, new password, confirm password. Uses supabase.auth.updateUser(). Reuse existing change password HTML/logic if possible, or duplicate the pattern

Activity section: 'View Activity' link that shows full transaction history. Filter chips: All, Graded, Adjustments, Settled. Transaction rows show: color indicator (green=win, red=loss, yellow=adjustment, purple=payment), enriched description, date, amount badge (player-facing: negated amounts). Settlement entries show bet context
Notification preferences: toggle switches for Pick Results (picks_graded), Balance Changes (balance_changes), Game Results (game_results). Same upsert pattern as organizer notification prefs
About section: links to Website, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy (open in new tabs)
Log Out button: confirmation, calls supabase.auth.signOut(), redirects to index.html
Delete Account button (muted danger text, at bottom): two-step confirmation (warning then type 'DELETE'). Calls delete_account edge function. Redirects to login on success
Add state: playerProfile (object), isLoadingPlayerAccount (boolean), playerActivityFilter ('all'), playerActivity (array)
Load player account data on route navigation
userStories.notes: Player name update: write to players table (display_name column) via Supabase. RLS requires using claim_player or similar — check if direct update works with player's auth. If not, the name might need an edge function. Email is read-only on web (email change requires auth confirmation flow which is complex). Activity amounts: NEGATE internal amounts for player display (internal positive = player owes bookie → display as negative/red for player). For transaction descriptions: ledger entries of type 'settlement' with a bet_id can be enriched by looking up the bet's side and grade_result.

userStories.title: Add persistent balance display in player header
userStories.description: As a player, I need to see my current balance at all times in the header, so I always know where I stand.
acceptanceCriteria: For player role: add balance display to the mobile header bar and desktop sidebar header area
Balance shown as large text, color-coded: green (positive = bookie owes player), red (negative = player owes bookie), gray (zero/settled)
Balance updates when navigating between views (computed from loaded ledger data)
On desktop sidebar: show balance below the user's name/email in the sidebar header
On mobile header: show balance on the right side of the top bar (next to hamburger menu)
Balance uses the player-facing convention: negate internal value (internal positive → display negative, internal negative → display positive)
Format as currency: '$1,234.56' with appropriate sign
Add computed getter 'playerDisplayBalance' that returns the negated formatted balance
Refresh balance when bet slip submission succeeds or when ledger data reloads via realtime
userStories.notes: The iOS app shows balance in AppHeaderView on every tab. For web, the sidebar or top bar is the equivalent. The balance should be reactive — when realtime subscription fires for ledger_entries changes, the balance updates automatically if the computed getter reads from the ledger data array. Make sure the realtime subscription for players also covers the player's own data, not just the bookie's data.
